The 162.9 reader_evidence covers only body lines 1-46 and annex lines 1-52 (C001-C002), but its assessment keys include all eleven components; C003-C011 are at body 47-196 and annex 53-315.

C006 sigma-finite assembly asserts without argument or cross-reference that the sets E_j intersected with D_i generate the trace sigma-field on D_i. No trace-sigma-field result was found in P15. This is a routine auxiliary fact, not the owed proof, so the verdict is unaffected.
def:p15-partition-averages never binds the notation E_nu(.|F_n), which body lines 73 and 88 use for the elementary average. Elsewhere in P15 that notation denotes general conditional expectation.

The independent uniform sequence space is used without a cross-reference to thm:p15-independent-sequence-existence (handbook/parts/p15/countable-product-measures.tex:135), which supplies it on the route.

The definition asserts, without showing it, that absolute continuity transfers between the binary-sequence-space laws and their real-sequence-space realization. C008's annex (lines 231-233) relies on this transfer when it invokes the R^N theorem thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion. The sentence also says that theorem 'applies' without stating the coordinatewise hypothesis alpha_m << beta_m, which C008's annex establishes first.
C010: 'its square is at most x-y' is stated without the one-line comparison (sqrt x - sqrt y <= sqrt x + sqrt y). The step is elementary and the verdict is unaffected.
